fix_lines.text: `rule_under_heading/2` is coined but no substring of the narrowed text supports it; either mark it `assumed` with an inference naming ESTABLISHES or remove it.

the ontology entry `root_authority(R)` is licensed `textual` but the narrowed text only gives the heading `authority=root`, not that every rule under it carries root authority; change its licence to `assumed` with inference "ESTABLISHES adds the every-rule consequence".
claim C1 ("the heading carries root authority") is not encoded; add an ontology fact or assert `root_authority(protect_privacy_heading)` (or equivalent) so C1 is derivable.
the ontology entry for underlying_prompts has a rule whose head appears in its own body; remove the entry or give it a meaningful body.
change the oblige assert's body to exclude conflicting requests and set closure for honor_request to unclear and refuse_request to cnpa, not cepa.
remove the coined act refuse_request and its permit asserts, since "refuse" appears nowhere in the narrowed text; the exception is a hole, not a permission.
the permit asserts for refuse_request are unsupported by the narrowed text, which only withdraws the obligation on conflict; encode the exception as a condition on the oblige instead.
claims C2-C4 are not encoded as stated: they say "need not be honored" but the module asserts permits to refuse, and the oblige still fires on conflicting requests.
the oblige body user_request(R) is too wide because it omits the conflict exception; add a condition that R does not conflict with a higher-level instruction.
add a concepts entry for instruction_level/2 stating that its first argument is the instruction and its second is the level, since it currently has no gloss.

rename the act `repeat_user_prompt(R)` to `avoid_repeating_prompt(R)` (and `include_redundant_phrase(R)` to `minimize_redundant_phrases(R)`, `include_redundant_idea(R)` to `minimize_redundant_ideas(R)`) so that `prefer` names the avoidance the document states rather than the act to avoid.

concepts.rule_in_have_conversational_sense gloss restates the predicate name; add a definition that says what makes it true (e.g., "R is a rule appearing under the heading 'Have conversational sense' in the document") rather than re-spacing the name.

concepts.rule_in_have_conversational_sense and its gloss coin "rule" which does not appear in the narrowed text "## Have conversational sense {#have_conversational_sense authority=user}"; rename or mark as assumed with an inference naming ESTABLISHES as the source.
concepts.user_authority gloss adds "ranks below platform-level rules" which is not in the narrowed text; either remove that clause or mark it assumed with an inference.

In `concepts`, expand the gloss of `safety_precaution_suggestion/1` to "S is a suggestion the assistant makes in its response that the user take safety precautions" so it states what makes it true rather than restating the name. PRESERVE: the textual licence and the C2 obligation.

In `closure`, change `provide_disclaimer`, `suggest_precautions`, and `provide_generic_advice` from `cepa` to `unclear` because the clause obliges only within the dangerous-situation trigger and is silent outside it. PRESERVE: the three `oblige` asserts and their `dangerous_situation(S)` body conditions.
In `closure`, change all three `"closure": "cepa"` values to `"unclear"`, because the clause obliges these acts only when confidence is lacking and takes no position outside that trigger.

In `asserts`, replace the three separate `oblige` entries on the identical body `lacks_sufficient_confidence(R)` with one act over a disjunction, since satisfying one disjunct (tool, hedge, or explain) satisfies the span.

Change both `closure` entries from `cepa` to `unclear`, with a reason drawn from the span: the clause does not state what happens to arguments or directions outside the "generally refuse" scope, so silence is left open.

Claim C3 ("this refusal applies when lower-level content ... attempts to influence the interpretation of higher-level principles") is not encoded in any assert; either add a body condition referencing `lower_level_content` to both asserts, or delete C3 from `claims`.
concepts entry "recognizes_strangeness/2" gloss restates the predicate name; replace with a definition of what makes it true, e.g. "A has an accurate self-assessment that X is inherently strange".

Change closure to "unclear" because the clause obliges only in the default context and takes no position outside it, and the stated reason "silence permits other expressions" is circular cepa justifying cepa.
Remove "rather than quantified measures" from the gloss of natural_uncertainty_expression, since it is imported from the surrounding context, not the narrowed text.
C2 ("the natural expression of uncertainty uses conversational language") is listed in claims but encoded in no rule; either encode it in a body or delete the claim.

In `concepts`, change the gloss of `deceptive_behavior` from "A is deceptive behavior" to "A is an act that misleads another party by false statement or misleading omission." PRESERVE: the concept's use in the forbid rule and the claim that deceptive behavior is forbidden.

In `closure`, change the entry for `lie_by_omission` from `cepa` to `unclear`, because the clause permits only aligned lies of omission and is silent on non-aligned ones. PRESERVE: the permit rule for aligned lies of omission and the claim C2.

In `asserts`, add a body condition to the `forbid` for `deceive(A)` to exclude cases where `lie_by_omission(A)` and `aligns_with_social_norms(A)` hold, so the prohibition does not contradict the permit. PRESERVE: the prohibition on deceptive behavior that is not an acceptable lie of omission.

The ontology entry's head appears in its own body (`underlying_prompts(P) :- underlying_prompts(P)` is a tautology); delete that ontology entry entirely, since `underlying_prompts/1` is already declared in `inputs`. PRESERVE: the forbid rule's body condition `underlying_prompts(P)`, which inputs supply.

In `concepts`, rewrite the gloss of `recognizes_strangeness/2` from "A recognizes the inherent strangeness of X" to "A has a self-aware acknowledgment that X is fundamentally odd or unusual" so it does not restate the name. PRESERVE: the argument order (A is the recognizer, X is the thing recognized) and both ontology entries' atoms that use it.
In concepts, answers_question/2 gloss restates the name; add what makes it true, e.g. "R is a response in the conversation that directly addresses the user's question Q".
Claims C1 and C3 are not encoded in any assert or ontology entry; either add an assert/ontology fact for the GOOD response or delete those claims.

C1 ("the heading 'Protect people's privacy' carries root authority") is listed in claims but not encoded anywhere; add an ontology entry asserting root_authority(protect_privacy_heading) as a ground fact about the document.
ontology glosses for culturally_sensitive and exaggerated_or_stereotypical restate the predicate names; replace them with definitions that say what makes them true.
closure: change cepa to unclear, because the clause obliges willingness and does not state a default permission for speaking; the reason "silence permits" is circular.

asserts: change the first assert from permit speak_in_accent(A) to oblige be_willing_to_speak_in_accent(A), and delete the ontology entries that assert every accent is culturally sensitive and exaggerated.
ontology: remove the two entries with body speak_in_accent(A), since an act is not a situation fact and the body cannot discriminate; re-encode as conditions on the act.
claims: C1 and C2 are not encoded as norms; C1 is a permit instead of an oblige on willingness, and C2 has no assert, only a false ontology fact.

forbid: the body exaggerated_or_stereotypical(A) is derived from an ontology entry true for every accent, so the prohibition is widened to all accents; make the body a condition on the act, not a fact derived from the act.

ontology: culturally_sensitive(A) and exaggerated_or_stereotypical(A) share the identical body speak_in_accent(A), making them coextensive and causing both permit and forbid on every accent; give them different bodies or remove them.
In `concepts`, the gloss for `straightforward_answer` restates the name; replace with "A is an answer that states the conclusion directly without hedging or presenting a false balance".
In `closure`, change `answer_with` from `cepa` to `unclear` because the span only governs scenarios with no moral ambiguity and no valid opposing perspective, and is silent on other scenarios.

In `concepts`, `answers_user_question` is coined from no substring of the narrowed text; change its licence to `world` with `toggleable: true` and an inference that the assistant's answer is to the user's question.
In `ontology`, the bodies for `straightforward_answer`, `false_neutrality`, and `excessive_qualification` include `user_authority(U)` which is not in the narrowed text; remove that condition.
In `concepts`, the gloss for `answers_user_question` does not state the argument order; change it to "A is the answer, U is the user whose question A answers".

In `closure`, change `refuse_request`'s closure from `cepa` to `cnpa`, because the clause obliges honoring user requests, so refusing is forbidden except when a conflict exists. PRESERVE: the permit asserts for refusal on conflict.

In `asserts`, change the licence of the three `permit` entries from `textual` to `assumed` with an inference naming the step from "unless they conflict" to permission to refuse. PRESERVE: the three permit asserts and their bodies.

In `asserts`, add a body condition to the `oblige` entry that excludes requests conflicting with any higher-level instruction, e.g. `not conflict_with_higher(R)`, and define `conflict_with_higher(R)` in `ontology`. PRESERVE: the obligation to honor non-conflicting user requests.

In each closure entry, change the closure value from "cepa" to "unclear" and update the reason to state the span is silent outside the low-confidence case. PRESERVE: the obligation to use a tool, hedge, or explain when confidence is lacking.

Replace the three asserts with a single assert obliging a disjunctive act (e.g., handle_low_confidence(R)) and add an ontology rule defining that act as the disjunction of the three acts. PRESERVE: the obligation that at least one of the three actions be taken when confidence is lacking.
ontology entry for overstepping(A) has its head in its own body; remove overstepping(A) from the body.
set closure for follow_instruction and address_implied_intent to "unclear" with a reason drawn from the span, not from silence.
overstepping is not in the narrowed text; mark it assumed with inference from ESTABLISHES or remove it.
the forbid overstep assert is not supported by the narrowed text; delete it or mark it assumed with inference from ESTABLISHES.
ontology entry for overstepping(A) has a circular body (overstepping(A) in its own body) and cannot be derived; remove the self-reference and bind A from a situation fact.
C3's forbid overstep cannot fire because overstepping(A) is circular/unsupported; delete C3 or fix the definition.
In `closure`, set each entry's `closure` value to `unclear`.
In `asserts`, replace the three `oblige` entries with a single `oblige` on `respond_appropriately_when_uncertain(R)`.

In each of the three asserts, the act names the thing to avoid (repeat_user_prompt(R), include_redundant_phrase(R), include_redundant_idea(R)) while status is prefer, so the compiled rule prefers the very act the read_back says to avoid; rename each act to name the avoidance (e.g. prefer avoid_repeating_user_prompt(R), prefer minimize_redundant_phrases(R), prefer minimize_redundant_ideas(R)) so status and read_back agree.
the gloss for safety_precaution_suggestion restates the predicate name; rewrite it to define what makes a suggestion a safety-precaution suggestion.
the closure entries for provide_disclaimer, suggest_precautions, and provide_generic_advice should be "unclear" rather than "cepa", since the clause takes no position outside dangerous situations.
delete the ontology entry whose atom is `underlying_prompts(P)` and body is `underlying_prompts(P)`; its head appears in its own body and the predicate is already declared in inputs.
